verses.text: A wise son heeds his father’s discipline, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.

xrefs.text: A fool rejects his father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.
He who corrects a mocker brings shame on himself; he who rebukes a wicked man taints himself.
A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man despises his mother.
Listen, my sons, to a father’s instruction; pay attention and gain understanding.
The proverbs of Solomon: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother.

verses.text: From the fruit of his lips a man enjoys good things, but the desire of the faithless is violence.

xrefs.text: By fruitful speech a man is filled with good things, and the work of his hands returns to him.
From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled; with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
So they will eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.
May no slanderer be established in the land; may calamity hunt down the man of violence.

verses.text: He who guards his mouth protects his life, but the one who opens his lips invites his own ruin.

xrefs.text: He who guards his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from distress.
Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
A fool’s mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
We all stumble in many ways. If anyone is never at fault in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole body.
For the choirmaster. For Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. I said, “I will watch my ways so that I will not sin with my tongue; I will guard my mouth with a muzzle as long as the wicked are present.”

verses.text: The slacker craves yet has nothing, but the soul of the diligent is fully satisfied.

xrefs.text: The hand of the diligent will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.
The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies lacks judgment.
For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue; and to virtue, knowledge;
if you incline your ear to wisdom and direct your heart to understanding,
Idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth.

verses.text: The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.

xrefs.text: Do not lie to one another, since you have taken off the old self with its practices,
Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to his neighbor, for we are all members of one another.
I hate and abhor falsehood, but Your law I love.
Then you will remember your evil ways and wicked deeds, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and abominations.
There you will remember your ways and all the deeds with which you have defiled yourselves, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evils you have done.

verses.text: Righteousness guards the man of integrity, but wickedness undermines the sinner.

xrefs.text: The integrity of the upright guides them, but the perversity of the faithless destroys them.
The righteousness of the blameless directs their path, but the wicked fall by their own wickedness.
May integrity and uprightness preserve me, because I wait for You.
May no slanderer be established in the land; may calamity hunt down the man of violence.
Of David. Vindicate me, O LORD! For I have walked with integrity; I have trusted in the LORD without wavering.

verses.text: One pretends to be rich, but has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.

xrefs.text: You say, ‘I am rich; I have grown wealthy and need nothing. But you do not realize that you are wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked.
The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, ‘God, I thank You that I am not like other men— swindlers, evildoers, adulterers— or even like this tax collector.
One gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds what is right, only to become poor.
Better to be lightly esteemed yet have a servant, than to be self-important but lack food.
Dishonest wealth will dwindle, but what is earned through hard work will be multiplied.

verses.text: Riches may ransom a man’s life, but a poor man hears no threat.

xrefs.text: What will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
For you know that it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed from the empty way of life you inherited from your forefathers,
He carried into exile all Jerusalem— all the commanders and mighty men of valor, all the craftsmen and metalsmiths— ten thousand captives in all. Only the poorest people of the land remained.
They trust in their wealth and boast in their great riches.
But Nebuzaradan left behind in the land of Judah some of the poor people who had no property, and at that time he gave them vineyards and fields.

verses.text: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.

xrefs.text: For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until midday.
Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.
Light shines on the righteous, gladness on the upright in heart.
Light dawns in the darkness for the upright— for the gracious, compassionate, and righteous.

verses.text: Arrogance leads only to strife, but wisdom is with the well-advised.

xrefs.text: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days.
The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but a wise man listens to counsel.
he is conceited and understands nothing. Instead, he has an unhealthy interest in controversies and disputes about words, out of which come envy, strife, abusive talk, evil suspicions,
To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.
What causes conflicts and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from the passions at war within you?

verses.text: Dishonest wealth will dwindle, but what is earned through hard work will be multiplied.

xrefs.text: An inheritance gained quickly will not be blessed in the end.
Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.
Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.
He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.
A faithful man will abound with blessings, but one eager to be rich will not go unpunished.

verses.text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.

xrefs.text: So also you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy.
Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is detestable to fools.
My soul faints for Your salvation; I wait for Your word.
I am weary from my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes fail, looking for my God.
Answer me quickly, O LORD; my spirit fails. Do not hide Your face from me, or I will be like those who descend to the Pit.

verses.text: He who despises instruction will pay the penalty, but the one who respects a command will be rewarded.

xrefs.text: He shall certainly be cut off, because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment; his guilt remains on him.”
But they mocked the messengers of God, despising His words and scoffing at His prophets, until the wrath of the LORD against His people was stirred up beyond remedy.
Abundant peace belongs to those who love Your law; nothing can make them stumble.
Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but that you may be fully rewarded.
because they kept rejecting My ordinances, refusing to walk in My statutes, and profaning My Sabbaths; for their hearts continually went after their idols.

verses.text: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.

xrefs.text: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man from the snares of death.
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
The cords of Sheol entangled me; the snares of death confronted me.
The cords of Sheol entangled me; the snares of death confronted me.
The ropes of death entangled me; the anguish of Sheol overcame me; I was confronted by trouble and sorrow.

verses.text: Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the faithless is difficult.

xrefs.text: Your own evil will discipline you; your own apostasies will reprimand you. Consider and realize how evil and bitter it is for you to forsake the LORD your God and to have no fear of Me,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.
But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; they do not know what makes them stumble.
Discipline is harsh for him who leaves the path; he who hates correction will die.
What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.
where your fathers tested and tried Me, though they had seen My work.

verses.text: Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool displays his folly.

xrefs.text: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.
Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the Lord’s will is.
Lying lips are detestable to the LORD, but those who deal faithfully are His delight.
Behold, My Servant will prosper; He will be raised and lifted up and highly exalted.
Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.

verses.text: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.

xrefs.text: Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the soul of his masters.
Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.
I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has strengthened me, that He considered me faithful and appointed me to service.
As for you, O son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; so hear the word from My mouth and give them the warning from Me.
Now it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

verses.text: Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.

xrefs.text: A fool rejects his father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.
He who listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.
Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates correction is stupid.
Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man’s rebuke to a listening ear.
He who despises instruction will pay the penalty, but the one who respects a command will be rewarded.

verses.text: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is detestable to fools.

xrefs.text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
“Sir, I answered, “you know. So he replied, “These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.”
Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.

verses.text: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.

xrefs.text: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
He who listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.
Leave your folly behind, and you will live; walk in the way of understanding.”
Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
I am a friend to all who fear You, and to those who keep Your precepts.

verses.text: Disaster pursues sinners, but prosperity is the reward of the righteous.

xrefs.text: Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but loving devotion surrounds him who trusts in the LORD.
Tell the righteous it will be well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of their labor.
He who despises instruction will pay the penalty, but the one who respects a command will be rewarded.
To those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life.
If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.”

verses.text: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.

xrefs.text: To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay,
He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.
I once was young and now am old, yet never have I seen the righteous abandoned or their children begging for bread.
His descendants will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.

verses.text: Abundant food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but without justice it is swept away.

xrefs.text: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies lacks judgment.
The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.
The produce of the earth is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.
Whoever keeps his command will come to no harm, and a wise heart knows the right time and procedure.
It is well with the man who is generous and lends freely, whose affairs are guided by justice.

verses.text: He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently.

xrefs.text: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
Do not withhold discipline from a child; although you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.
Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be party to his death.
Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.

verses.text: A righteous man eats to his heart’s content, but the stomach of the wicked is empty.

xrefs.text: Young lions go lacking and hungry, but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.
The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but He denies the craving of the wicked.
Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have, for God has said: “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you.”
For physical exercise is of limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come.
They will be wasted from hunger and ravaged by pestilence and bitter plague; I will send the fangs of wild beasts against them, with the venom of vipers that slither in the dust.
